limits: No rendered/manual driving acceptance, wall corners, slopes, airborne obstacle contacts, chain car collisions or full network disturbances/four players.
Native aerial network fixture demonstrates actual reverse motion/replication, not identical visually sampled peak speeds on both peers or guaranteed final wall clearance.
Distance starts at authority bounce execution; scan may first observe a full crossing. No teleport to original contact plane.
Natural pillar collisions can still rotate or flip cars. Bounce Back itself never writes angular velocity.
New reflection/history payload requires same rebuilt code on all peers; team must manually recompile/save Blueprint. No asset edits, commit or push.
